issues.legal_issue: A court must make a fact-specific inquiry into partial eviction before ordering eviction from the entire premises when the landlord’s need is proved and the tenant agrees to continue in part; it cannot presume that partial eviction is impracticable merely because the premises comprise one room.
material_facts: The premises consisted of a shop measuring 24 by 22 feet with an attached verandah measuring 6 by 22 feet, where the tenant operated a restaurant.
The landlord sought eviction to meet his need for a son to start a television shop, and that need was found proved.
The tenant indicated agreement to continue in occupation of part of the premises, but the landlord did not agree to dividing the premises into two equal halves.

The lower courts ordered eviction from the entire premises without examining whether partial eviction could substantially satisfy the landlord’s need; the High Court relied on a presumption that partial eviction would not suffice where the premises comprised one shop room.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed, the orders for eviction from the entire premises were set aside to that extent, and the matter was remitted for an inquiry into whether the premises could be divided so that eviction from only part would substantially satisfy the landlord’s need.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to Section 11(1)(c) of the Bihar Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1982 requires the court, after finding the landlord’s need proved, to consider whether that need may be substantially satisfied by evicting the tenant from only part of the premises, where the tenant agrees to continue in the remainder. Whether partial eviction is practicable is a question of fact in each case; the fact that premises comprise one room does not create a presumption that partial eviction cannot be ordered. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_case and landlord_need_proved and tenant_agrees_to_partial_occupation and full_eviction_ordered_without_partial_inquiry

predicates.rent_control_eviction_case: The proceeding is a rent-control case seeking eviction of a tenant from premises.
predicates.landlord_need_proved: The court has found the landlord’s stated need for occupation of the premises proved.
predicates.tenant_agrees_to_partial_occupation: The tenant agrees to continue occupying the remainder if evicted from part of the premises.
predicates.full_eviction_ordered_without_partial_in: The court ordered eviction from the entire premises without examining whether eviction from only part could substantially satisfy the landlord’s need.

issues.definition: When the landlord’s need is proved and the tenant agrees to remain in part of the premises, a court in a rent-control eviction case that has ordered full eviction without assessing partial eviction must examine whether partial eviction would substantially satisfy that need before ordering eviction from the whole premises.
